verses.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς Ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν πλούσιος ὃς εἶχεν οἰκονόμον καὶ οὗτος διεβλήθη αὐτῷ ὡς διασκορπίζων τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Elegen de kai pros tous mathētas Anthrōpos tis ēn plousios hos eichen oikonomon kai houtos dieblēthē autō hōs diaskorpizōn ta hyparchonta autou
verses.literal: Jesus also said to His disciples There was a rich man whose manager was accused of . . . . . . . . . wasting his possessions

verses.original: καὶ φωνήσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν αὐτῷ Τί τοῦτο ἀκούω περὶ σοῦ ἀπόδος τὸν λόγον τῆς οἰκονομίας σου οὐ γὰρ δύνῃ ἔτι οἰκονομεῖν
verses.transliteration: kai phōnēsas auton eipen autō Ti touto akouō peri sou apodos ton logon tēs oikonomias sou ou gar dynē eti oikonomein
verses.literal: So he called him in to ask What is this I hear about you Turn in an account of your management for you cannot . . . be manager any longer

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ἐν ἑαυτῷ ὁ οἰκονόμος Τί ποιήσω ὅτι ὁ κύριός μου ἀφαιρεῖται τὴν οἰκονομίαν ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ σκάπτειν οὐκ ἰσχύω ἐπαιτεῖν αἰσχύνομαι
verses.transliteration: Eipen de en heautō ho oikonomos Ti poiēsō hoti ho kyrios mou aphaireitai tēn oikonomian ap’ emou skaptein ouk ischyō epaitein aischynomai
verses.literal: The manager said to himself What shall I do now that my master is taking away my position I am too weak to dig and too ashamed to beg

verses.original: ἔγνων τί ποιήσω ἵνα ὅταν μετασταθῶ ἐκ τῆς οἰκονομίας δέξωνταί με εἰς τοὺς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν
verses.transliteration: egnōn ti poiēsō hina hotan metastathō ek tēs oikonomias dexōntai me eis tous oikous heautōn
verses.literal: I know what I will do so that after my removal from management people will welcome me into their homes

verses.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος ἕνα ἕκαστον τῶν χρεοφειλετῶν τοῦ κυρίου ἑαυτοῦ ἔλεγεν τῷ πρώτῳ Πόσον ὀφείλεις τῷ κυρίῳ μου
verses.transliteration: Kai proskalesamenos hena hekaston tōn chreopheiletōn tou kyriou heautou elegen tō prōtō Poson opheileis tō kyriō mou
verses.literal: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors How much do you owe . . . my master he asked the first

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν βάτους ἐλαίου Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ καθίσας ταχέως γράψον πεντήκοντα
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Hekaton batous elaiou Ho de eipen autō Dexai sou ta grammata kai kathisas tacheōs grapson pentēkonta
verses.literal: A hundred measures of olive oil - he answered Take your bill - said the manager - sit down quickly and write fifty

verses.original: Ἔπειτα ἑτέρῳ εἶπεν Σὺ δὲ πόσον ὀφείλεις Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἑκατὸν κόρους σίτου Λέγει αὐτῷ Δέξαι σου τὰ γράμματα καὶ γράψον ὀγδοήκοντα
verses.transliteration: Epeita heterō eipen Sy de poson opheileis Ho de eipen Hekaton korous sitou Legei autō Dexai sou ta grammata kai grapson ogdoēkonta
verses.literal: Then he asked another And how much do you owe A hundred measures of wheat - he replied Take your bill and write eighty he told him

verses.original: Καὶ ἐπῄνεσεν ὁ κύριος τὸν οἰκονόμον τῆς ἀδικίας ὅτι φρονίμως ἐποίησεν ὅτι οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου φρονιμώτεροι ὑπὲρ τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ φωτὸς εἰς τὴν γενεὰν τὴν ἑαυτῶν εἰσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai epēnesen ho kyrios ton oikonomon tēs adikias hoti phronimōs epoiēsen hoti hoi huioi tou aiōnos toutou phronimōteroi hyper tous huious tou phōtos eis tēn genean tēn heautōn eisin
verses.literal: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light

verses.original: Καὶ ἐγὼ ὑμῖν λέγω ἑαυτοῖς ποιήσατε φίλους ἐκ τοῦ μαμωνᾶ τῆς ἀδικίας ἵνα ὅταν ἐκλίπῃ δέξωνται ὑμᾶς εἰς τὰς αἰωνίους σκηνάς
verses.transliteration: Kai egō hymin legō heautois poiēsate philous ek tou mamōna tēs adikias hina hotan eklipē dexōntai hymas eis tas aiōnious skēnas
verses.literal: I tell you use - worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves so that when it is gone they will welcome you into eternal dwellings

verses.original: Ὁ πιστὸς ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ καὶ ἐν πολλῷ πιστός ἐστιν καὶ ὁ ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ ἄδικος καὶ ἐν πολλῷ ἄδικός ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: Ho pistos en elachistō kai en pollō pistos estin kai ho en elachistō adikos kai en pollō adikos estin
verses.literal: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much

verses.original: εἰ οὖν ἐν τῷ ἀδίκῳ μαμωνᾷ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε τὸ ἀληθινὸν τίς ὑμῖν πιστεύσει
verses.transliteration: ei oun en tō adikō mamōna pistoi ouk egenesthe to alēthinon tis hymin pisteusei
verses.literal: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth who will entrust you with true riches

verses.original: καὶ εἰ ἐν τῷ ἀλλοτρίῳ πιστοὶ οὐκ ἐγένεσθε τὸ ὑμέτερον τίς δώσει ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: kai ei en tō allotriō pistoi ouk egenesthe to hymeteron tis dōsei hymin
verses.literal: And if you have not been faithful with the belongings of another who will give you belongings of your own

verses.original: Οὐδεὶς οἰκέτης δύναται δυσὶ κυρίοις δουλεύειν ἢ γὰρ τὸν ἕνα μισήσει καὶ τὸν ἕτερον ἀγαπήσει ἢ ἑνὸς ἀνθέξεται καὶ τοῦ ἑτέρου καταφρονήσει οὐ δύνασθε Θεῷ δουλεύειν καὶ μαμωνᾷ
verses.transliteration: Oudeis oiketēs dynatai dysi kyriois douleuein ē gar ton hena misēsei kai ton heteron agapēsei ē henos anthexetai kai tou heterou kataphronēsei ou dynasthe Theō douleuein kai mamōna
verses.literal: No servant can serve two masters Either he will hate the one and love the other or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other You cannot serve both God and money

verses.original: Ἤκουον δὲ ταῦτα πάντα οἱ Φαρισαῖοι φιλάργυροι ὑπάρχοντες καὶ ἐξεμυκτήριζον αὐτόν
verses.transliteration: Ēkouon de tauta panta hoi Pharisaioi philargyroi hyparchontes kai exemyktērizon auton
verses.literal: The Pharisees who were lovers of money heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμεῖς ἐστε οἱ δικαιοῦντες ἑαυτοὺς ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὁ δὲ Θεὸς γινώσκει τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν ὅτι τὸ ἐν ἀνθρώποις ὑψηλὸν βδέλυγμα ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai eipen autois Hymeis este hoi dikaiountes heautous enōpion tōn anthrōpōn ho de Theos ginōskei tas kardias hymōn hoti to en anthrōpois hypsēlon bdelygma enōpion tou Theou
verses.literal: So He said to them You are the ones who justify yourselves before men but God knows your hearts For what is prized among men is detestable before God

verses.original: Ὁ νόμος καὶ οἱ προφῆται μέχρι Ἰωάννου ἀπὸ τότε ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ εὐαγγελίζεται καὶ πᾶς εἰς αὐτὴν βιάζεται
verses.transliteration: Ho nomos kai hoi prophētai mechri Iōannou apo tote hē basileia tou Theou euangelizetai kai pas eis autēn biazetai
verses.literal: The Law and the Prophets were proclaimed until John Since that time the gospel of the kingdom of God is being preached and everyone is forcing his way into it

verses.original: εὐκοπώτερον δέ ἐστιν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν παρελθεῖν ἢ τοῦ νόμου μίαν κεραίαν πεσεῖν
verses.transliteration: eukopōteron de estin ton ouranon kai tēn gēn parelthein ē tou nomou mian keraian pesein
verses.literal: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law

verses.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἀπολύων τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ καὶ γαμῶν ἑτέραν μοιχεύει καὶ ὁ ἀπολελυμένην ἀπὸ ἀνδρὸς γαμῶν μοιχεύει
verses.transliteration: Pas ho apolyōn tēn gynaika autou kai gamōn heteran moicheuei kai ho apolelymenēn apo andros gamōn moicheuei
verses.literal: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery and he who marries a divorced woman . . . . . . commits adultery

verses.original: Ἄνθρωπος δέ τις ἦν πλούσιος καὶ ἐνεδιδύσκετο πορφύραν καὶ βύσσον εὐφραινόμενος καθ’ ἡμέραν λαμπρῶς
verses.transliteration: Anthrōpos de tis ēn plousios kai enedidysketo porphyran kai bysson euphrainomenos kath’ hēmeran lamprōs
verses.literal: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen who lived each day in joyous . . . . . . splendor

verses.original: πτωχὸς δέ τις ὀνόματι Λάζαρος ἐβέβλητο πρὸς τὸν πυλῶνα αὐτοῦ εἱλκωμένος
verses.transliteration: ptōchos de tis onomati Lazaros ebeblēto pros ton pylōna autou heilkōmenos
verses.literal: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate covered with sores

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιθυμῶν χορτασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν πιπτόντων ἀπὸ τῆς τραπέζης τοῦ πλουσίου ἀλλὰ καὶ οἱ κύνες ἐρχόμενοι ἐπέλειχον τὰ ἕλκη αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai epithymōn chortasthēnai apo tōn piptontōn apo tēs trapezēs tou plousiou alla kai hoi kynes erchomenoi epeleichon ta helkē autou
verses.literal: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table Even the dogs came and licked his sores

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἀποθανεῖν τὸν πτωχὸν καὶ ἀπενεχθῆναι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀγγέλων εἰς τὸν κόλπον Ἀβραάμ ἀπέθανεν δὲ καὶ ὁ πλούσιος καὶ ἐτάφη
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de apothanein ton ptōchon kai apenechthēnai auton hypo tōn angelōn eis ton kolpon Abraam apethanen de kai ho plousios kai etaphē
verses.literal: One day . . . the beggar died and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side And the rich man also died and was buried

verses.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ ᾅδῃ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχων ἐν βασάνοις ὁρᾷ Ἀβραὰμ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν καὶ Λάζαρον ἐν τοῖς κόλποις αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai en tō hadē eparas tous ophthalmous autou hyparchōn en basanois hora Abraam apo makrothen kai Lazaron en tois kolpois autou
verses.literal: In Hades where he was in torment he looked up . . . . . . . . . and saw Abraham from afar with Lazarus by his side

verses.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς φωνήσας εἶπεν Πάτερ Ἀβραάμ ἐλέησόν με καὶ πέμψον Λάζαρον ἵνα βάψῃ τὸ ἄκρον τοῦ δακτύλου αὐτοῦ ὕδατος καὶ καταψύξῃ τὴν γλῶσσάν μου ὅτι ὀδυνῶμαι ἐν τῇ φλογὶ ταύτῃ
verses.transliteration: Kai autos phōnēsas eipen Pater Abraam eleēson me kai pempson Lazaron hina bapsē to akron tou daktylou autou hydatos kai katapsyxē tēn glōssan mou hoti odynōmai en tē phlogi tautē
verses.literal: So he cried out . . . Father Abraham have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue For I am in agony in this fire

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ Ἀβραάμ Τέκνον μνήσθητι ὅτι ἀπέλαβες τὰ ἀγαθά σου ἐν τῇ ζωῇ σου καὶ Λάζαρος ὁμοίως τὰ κακά νῦν δὲ ὧδε παρακαλεῖται σὺ δὲ ὀδυνᾶσαι
verses.transliteration: Eipen de Abraam Teknon mnēsthēti hoti apelabes ta agatha sou en tē zōē sou kai Lazaros homoiōs ta kaka nyn de hōde parakaleitai sy de odynasai
verses.literal: But Abraham answered Child remember that during your lifetime you received your good things while Lazarus received bad things But now he is comforted here while you are in agony

verses.original: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις μεταξὺ ἡμῶν καὶ ὑμῶν χάσμα μέγα ἐστήρικται ὅπως οἱ θέλοντες διαβῆναι ἔνθεν πρὸς ὑμᾶς μὴ δύνωνται μηδὲ ἐκεῖθεν πρὸς ἡμᾶς διαπερῶσιν
verses.transliteration: kai en pasi toutois metaxy hēmōn kai hymōn chasma mega estēriktai hopōs hoi thelontes diabēnai enthen pros hymas mē dynōntai mēde ekeithen pros hēmas diaperōsin
verses.literal: And besides all this a great chasm has been fixed between us and you so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you nor can anyone cross from there to us

verses.original: Εἶπεν δέ Ἐρωτῶ σε οὖν πάτερ ἵνα πέμψῃς αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός μου
verses.transliteration: Eipen de Erōtō se oun pater hina pempsēs auton eis ton oikon tou patros mou
verses.literal: Then I beg you father he said send Lazarus to my father’s house

verses.original: ἔχω γὰρ πέντε ἀδελφούς ὅπως διαμαρτύρηται αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλθωσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦτον τῆς βασάνου
verses.transliteration: echō gar pente adelphous hopōs diamartyrētai autois hina mē kai autoi elthōsin eis ton topon touton tēs basanou
verses.literal: for I have five brothers Let him warn them so that they will not also end up in this place of torment

verses.original: Λέγει δὲ Ἀβραάμ Ἔχουσι Μωϋσέα καὶ τοὺς προφήτας ἀκουσάτωσαν αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Legei de Abraam Echousi Mōusea kai tous prophētas akousatōsan autōn
verses.literal: But Abraham replied They have Moses and the Prophets let your brothers listen to them

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Οὐχί πάτερ Ἀβραάμ ἀλλ’ ἐάν τις ἀπὸ νεκρῶν πορευθῇ πρὸς αὐτοὺς μετανοήσουσιν
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Ouchi pater Abraam all’ ean tis apo nekrōn poreuthē pros autous metanoēsousin
verses.literal: No father Abraham - he said but if someone is sent to them from the dead they will repent

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ Εἰ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν προφητῶν οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδ’ ἐάν τις ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῇ πεισθήσονται
verses.transliteration: Eipen de autō Ei Mōuseōs kai tōn prophētōn ouk akouousin oud’ ean tis ek nekrōn anastē peisthēsontai
verses.literal: Then Abraham said to him If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead
